title: PE filename selection
description: Selects a bounded Content-Disposition filename, with UTF-8 extended parameter precedence, explicit language syntax, duplicate checks and byte level filename restrictions.

topics.title: Bound retained PE headers
topics.description: max_prefix_bytes limits each retained header prefix to 65536 bytes. needed returns a value beyond this cap for an unusable prefix, and main rejects it before copying more bytes.

links.label: Apply the prefix cap before copying

topics.title: Bound active file contexts
topics.description: max_active_contexts permits 128 simultaneous admitted contexts. Main checks this count before allocating shared HTTP and file state.

topics.title: Bound header value bytes
topics.description: max_header_value_bytes is 4096. Main checks each response header value, decimal_length bounds the stripped decimal input, and the filename and language parsers use the same byte cap.

topics.title: Bound selected name bytes
topics.description: max_filename_bytes caps a meaningful filename at 255 bytes. The bound applies to decoded filename* bytes or the selected ordinary filename.

topics.title: Bound distinct parameters
topics.description: max_parameters permits 16 distinct parameter names. The parser checks the set size before adding the next lowercased key.

topics.title: Bound PE section count
topics.description: max_sections permits 96 COFF section entries. pe_format checks the count and the complete table extent before reading section fields.

topics.title: Bound declared object bytes
topics.description: max_object_bytes is 268435456 bytes. decimal_length bounds the parsed Content-Length with checked accumulation; pe_format also checks its declared argument against this cap.

topics.title: Export the filename selector
topics.description: The exported function declaration gives selected_filename a string input and string result. The implementation returns the selected name or an empty string that prevents admission in main.
links: Open the actual filename parser definition

links.label: Send the header value to the selector

topics.title: Read one byte as a count
topics.description: octet translates a zero based index i to sub_bytes offset i+1, reads one byte and converts that byte string to a count. UTF-8 checks, filename byte restrictions and decimal parsing use this numeric byte value.

ranges.code:
function octet(s: string, i: count): count
{ return bytestring_to_count(sub_bytes(s, i+1, 1)); }

links: Use numeric bytes for UTF-8 classes
Use numeric bytes for filename restrictions

links.label: Use a numeric byte as a decimal digit

topics.title: Select bytes at a zero based offset
topics.description: part translates offset i to the one based sub_bytes interface and requests n bytes. Filename parsing uses it for characters and spans; PE helpers use it for signatures and integer fields.

ranges.code:
function part(s: string, i: count, n: count): string
{ return sub_bytes(s, i+1, n); }

links.label: Pass a selected byte span into integer decoding
Copy only the current required prefix span

topics.title: Recognize an HTTP token byte
topics.description: The anchored character class accepts exactly one HTTP token character, including ASCII letters, digits and the listed punctuation. Disposition, parameter keys and unquoted values advance only through bytes accepted here.

ranges.code:
function token(c: string): bool
{ return /^[!#$%&'*+.^_`|~0-9A-Za-z-]$/ == c; }

topics.title: Walk the candidate UTF-8 bytes
topics.description: utf8_ok starts at byte zero and advances through the complete byte string. It is called on decoded extended names and, after extended selection, on the ordinary fallback.

topics.title: Accept a single ASCII byte
topics.description: octet reads the next numeric byte and i advances once. Bytes below 128 need no continuation and move directly to the next character.

topics.title: Set the normal continuation range
topics.description: Continuation bytes normally range from 128 through 191. n will hold how many continuation bytes follow the leading byte; lo and hi constrain the first continuation.

ranges.code: local n: count; local lo: count=128; local hi: count=191;

topics.title: Accept a two byte leading class
topics.description: Leading bytes 194 through 223 require one continuation. Starting at 194 excludes the C0 and C1 leads that would encode an ASCII value with an overlong representation.

topics.title: Constrain three byte sequences
topics.description: Leading bytes 224 through 239 require two continuations. E0 raises the first continuation minimum to 160 to exclude overlong encodings; ED lowers its maximum to 159 to exclude surrogate code points.

topics.title: Constrain four byte sequences
topics.description: Leading bytes 240 through 244 require three continuations. F0 raises the first continuation minimum to 144 and F4 lowers its maximum to 143, keeping the represented value from U+10000 through U+10FFFF.

topics.title: Reject other leading bytes
topics.description: A byte outside ASCII and the accepted multibyte leading classes returns F. This includes a continuation byte in leading position and lead bytes above F4.

topics.title: Require the first continuation in bounds
topics.description: The remaining byte count must contain all n continuations. octet at i must satisfy the first continuation range selected for this lead, then i advances.

ranges.code:
if ( i+n > |s| || octet(s,i)<lo || octet(s,i)>hi ) return F;
++i;

topics.title: Require every later continuation
topics.description: While more than one continuation remains, each following byte must be 128 through 191. Each accepted byte advances i and reduces n.

ranges.code:
while ( n>1 )
{ if ( octet(s,i)<128 || octet(s,i)>191 ) return F; ++i; --n; }

topics.title: Return complete byte validation
topics.description: T means the loop consumed the entire candidate with accepted ASCII bytes or valid bounded continuation sequences. The caller uses this boolean to decide whether the name can be selected.
links: Use UTF-8 validity for the ordinary name

topics.title: Require a bounded basename
topics.description: meaningful requires 1 through 255 bytes and rejects a leading or trailing ASCII space or dot. The selected value therefore has a nonempty bounded basename with explicit edge restrictions.
links: Apply to the selected ordinary name

topics.title: Inspect every filename byte
topics.description: The loop reads each byte numerically through octet, incrementing i once per byte. It checks the byte representation passed in, including bytes produced by URI unescaping.

topics.title: Exclude controls and path separators
topics.description: The byte predicate rejects C0 controls below 32, DEL 127, slash 47, backslash 92 and colon 58. These checks keep selected names from carrying these path and control bytes.

topics.title: Return accepted basename restrictions
topics.description: T reports that every byte and the edge and length checks passed. UTF-8 validity is checked separately by the caller before a selected name reaches main.
links: Combine byte restrictions with extended UTF-8
Combine byte restrictions with ordinary UTF-8

topics.title: Accept an absent RFC8187 language
topics.description: language_ok immediately accepts an empty language component. selected_filename extracts this optional component between the two apostrophes in the UTF-8 extended value.
links: Pass the extracted language into this definition

topics.title: Bound and lowercase the language
topics.description: The shared header cap bounds language byte length. to_lower produces tag for case insensitive grammar, grandfathered membership and duplicate checks.

topics.title: List the grandfathered language forms
topics.description: The explicit set contains the RFC5646 grandfathered forms, including en-gb-oed, the listed i and sgn forms, and the listed art, cel, no and zh forms. Membership is tested after lowercasing, so spelling case does not change selection.

topics.title: Accept a listed grandfathered tag
topics.description: A lowercased tag in grandfathered returns T before the general grammar. These explicit legacy forms therefore have a defined acceptance path.

ranges.code: if ( tag in grandfathered ) return T;

links: Read the exact accepted legacy set

topics.title: Accept a private use language form
topics.description: The anchored pattern accepts x followed by one or more subtags, each containing 1 through 8 ASCII letters or digits. A bare x has no following subtag and fails this pattern.

topics.title: Require the language tag grammar
topics.description: The anchored grammar accepts a two or three letter primary with up to three three letter extlangs, or a four through eight letter primary. An optional four letter script and two letter or three digit region precede variants of five through eight alphanumerics, or a digit plus three alphanumerics. Each extension has a digit or letter singleton other than x and one or more two through eight character alphanumeric subtags. An optional final x group contains one or more one through eight character private use subtags.

topics.title: Advance past language script and region
topics.description: After the whole tag matches the grammar, splitting on hyphens lets the duplicate checks locate later fields. The cursor skips the primary, permitted extlangs, an optional four letter script and an optional two letter or three digit region.

topics.title: Track variant subtags
topics.description: A fresh variants set records the lowercased variants. The loop recognizes the same variant forms used in the full grammar before moving to extension singletons.

ranges.code:
local variants: set[string]=set();
while ( i<|subtags| && /^([a-z0-9]{5,8}|[0-9][a-z0-9]{3})$/ == subtags[i] )

topics.title: Require distinct variant subtags
topics.description: A repeated variant returns F. Each first occurrence is added to the set and advances the subtag cursor, making case variations of one variant count as a duplicate.

ranges.code:
if ( subtags[i] in variants ) return F;
add variants[subtags[i]]; ++i;

topics.title: Track extension singleton keys
topics.description: The singleton set is separate from variants. The remaining subtag loop visits extension singleton keys and the optional final private use marker.

topics.title: Finish at the private use tail
topics.description: When the current subtag is x, the already matched private use tail permits an immediate T. Private use contents are outside the extension singleton duplicate set.

topics.title: Require distinct extension keys
topics.description: A repeated singleton returns F. Each accepted key enters singletons; the cursor then skips its subtags until the next one character key, whose uniqueness is checked on the next iteration.

topics.title: Return accepted language syntax
topics.description: T reaches the extended filename parser after grammar and duplicate checks complete. The language component qualifies the parameter syntax; the selected filename remains the decoded encoded component.

topics.title: Enter bounded filename selection
topics.description: selected_filename accepts the complete Content-Disposition value and returns an empty string for an empty value or one above 4096 bytes. Main stores the returned string as the advertised filename and requires it to be nonempty for file admission.

links.label: Return the selected name to response header state

topics.title: Skip leading header whitespace
topics.description: The parser initializes a zero based byte cursor, skips ASCII space and tab, and marks start for the disposition token.
links: Read whitespace using zero based byte slices

topics.title: Read and lowercase the disposition
topics.description: token(part(value,i,1)) advances through HTTP token bytes. part extracts that span and to_lower supplies the disposition used by the following admission guard.

topics.title: Select attachment or inline
topics.description: Only attachment and inline dispositions proceed to parameter selection. Any other token or an empty token returns an empty result.

topics.title: Keep distinct keys and candidate names
topics.description: params records every lowercased parameter key, including unrecognized keys. plain and extended start empty and retain the ordinary and RFC8187 filename candidates while the entire parameter list is parsed.

ranges.code:
local params: set[string]=set(); local plain=""; local extended="";
while ( i<|value| )

topics.title: Require semicolons between parameters
topics.description: Space and tab are skipped at each list boundary. Reaching the end finishes the list; otherwise a semicolon is required, followed by optional space or tab before the next key.

topics.title: Require a token parameter key
topics.description: The key starts at the current cursor and consumes token bytes. An empty key returns an empty selection. Lowercasing makes later duplicate and filename comparisons case insensitive.

topics.title: Admit only the exact filename* key
topics.description: A key beginning filename* is accepted only when it equals filename*. This excludes numbered or other suffixed continuation forms from the supported extended parameter grammar.

topics.title: Bound and deduplicate all keys
topics.description: An already present key or a seventeenth distinct key returns an empty selection. The accepted key enters params before its value is parsed, so duplicates of ordinary, extended and unrecognized parameters all affect admission.

ranges.code:
if ( key in params || |params|>=max_parameters ) return "";
add params[key];

topics.title: Require an equals sign and initialize the value
topics.description: Space and tab may surround the required equals sign. v starts empty and quoted starts F for each parameter. These flags later distinguish an ordinary quoted string from an extended value, which must be unquoted.

topics.title: Enter a quoted parameter value
topics.description: An opening double quote sets quoted, consumes the quote and starts a byte loop with closed=F. A closing double quote must be seen for this form to complete.

topics.title: Close at an unescaped double quote
topics.description: Each byte is read and consumed. An unescaped double quote sets closed=T and exits the loop; it is not appended to the stored value.

ranges.code:
local c=part(value,i,1); ++i;
if ( c=="\"" ) { closed=T; break; }

topics.title: Consume a quoted pair
topics.description: A backslash requires one following byte and replaces c with that byte. A trailing backslash returns an empty selection. The following control check and append apply to the unescaped byte.

ranges.code:
if ( c=="\\" )
{ if ( i==|value| ) return ""; c=part(value,i,1); ++i; }

topics.title: Check and append quoted bytes
topics.description: The quoted string path excludes NUL through backspace, LF through unit separator and DEL, while allowing horizontal tab at this syntax step. Accepted bytes are appended to v; selected filename restrictions later reject tab too.

topics.title: Require a closing quote
topics.description: Exhausting the input before closed becomes T returns an empty selection. A complete quoted value resumes parsing at the byte after the closing quote.

topics.title: Read a nonempty unquoted token value
topics.description: The unquoted path consumes HTTP token bytes, rejects an empty span and assigns the complete span to v. The next list iteration requires only whitespace, end of input or a semicolon after this span.

topics.title: Retain the ordinary filename candidate
topics.description: The filename parameter assigns its parsed value to plain. Final selection first checks whether filename* was present, so this ordinary candidate is used only when no extended parameter was supplied.

topics.title: Require the UTF-8 extended value form
topics.description: filename* enters a separate branch. It must be unquoted and begin with case insensitive UTF-8, an apostrophe, an optional language containing ASCII letters, digits or hyphens, and another apostrophe. Later checks validate the complete encoded component.

topics.title: Validate the extracted language component
topics.description: The nested substitutions select the language between the first and second apostrophes. language_ok must return T; F returns an empty filename selection before decoding the name.
links: Pass the language into its actual validator definition

topics.title: Require attr-char bytes or complete escapes
topics.description: Removing the charset and language prefix yields encoded. Its anchored grammar accepts only RFC8187 attr-char bytes and percent escapes with two hexadecimal digits, so incomplete escapes and raw bytes outside that alphabet return an empty selection.

topics.title: Decode the extended name bytes
topics.description: unescape_URI converts the validated percent escapes into extended bytes. The next checks operate on that decoded byte string, including any encoded separators or controls.

topics.title: Require valid UTF-8 and meaningful decoded bytes
topics.description: utf8_ok and meaningful must both accept extended. Either failure returns an empty selection, including when an ordinary filename parameter was also supplied.
links: Validate decoded UTF-8 at the helper definition
Check decoded name length edges and path bytes

topics.title: Return filename* before examining the fallback
topics.description: Presence of filename* returns the validated extended value immediately. This happens before meaningful(plain) and utf8_ok(plain), so a valid extended name wins even when an ignored ordinary fallback has unsafe or unsupported bytes.

links.label: Store the selected extended name in main

topics.title: Check the ordinary name when it is selected
topics.description: When filename* is absent and filename exists, meaningful must accept plain. An unsafe ordinary name therefore returns empty only on the ordinary selection path.

topics.title: Validate the selected ordinary byte encoding
topics.description: The final ordinary selection path requires utf8_ok(plain). This accepts UTF-8 ordinary bytes and runs only after extended precedence has already returned.
links: Validate ordinary UTF-8 at the helper definition

topics.title: Return the ordinary selection
topics.description: plain becomes the selected name when no filename* was supplied and the ordinary checks passed. If neither name was supplied, plain remains empty and main declines file admission.

links.label: Return ordinary name bytes to main
Use the nonempty selected name for admission
